reviewed_assertions: tests/test_drain_week_view.py:68 checks that fixture construction yields 120 records; it fails if the fixture size changes and is not counted as a product guard.

tests/test_drain_week_view.py:94-130 compares returned phase counts, held reasons, launches, landings and estimates against literal expected values; removing a phase bucket, changing a reason count, or using the wrong denominator makes a corresponding assertion fail.
tests/test_drain_week_view.py:131-136 requires the later of two verdicts and excludes ordinary pending upstream waits; taking the first log entry or listing all old waits makes it fail.

tests/test_drain_week_view.py:180-197 first verifies ready, pending and failed dependency outcomes against independent literals from the admission resolver, establishing the fixture's known present controls.

tests/test_drain_week_view.py:211-214 requires ready and failed old waits, with separate literal verdicts; reverting the failed-transition repair omits r-blocked and fails, as blocked-upstream-negative-control.log shows.
tests/test_drain_week_view.py:243-245 fails if a landed run uses its old dispatch stamp for recent launches or omits a recent landing.
tests/test_drain_week_view.py:252 fails if zero landings produces an estimate or raises on division.
tests/test_drain_week_view.py:267-270 requires 250 queued and 250 upstream pointers in both MCP calls and fails if either call takes 30 seconds or more.

No added assertion compares a returned value with the same mutable value passed to the code under test; the expected phase counts, outcomes, stamps and verdicts are literals or separately specified fixture facts.
